transcript:
Header: 2026-04-10 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Avery (Nebula Head of ML), Marcus (Infra), Priya (Product)

Summary: high-level discovery focused on per-token economics, tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, batching and caching levers, budget constraints, and a request to run a small benchmark.

00:00 Sofia: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm so excited to chat through what you're trying to solve for w/ Nebula, can folks do quick intros?
00:10 Avery: hey i'm avery, head of ml, we run a conversational assistant and a summarization pipeline, biggest issues are cost predictability and latency spikes during peak hours
00:18 Marcus: marcus infra, we manage their k8s clusters and internal GPU pool, interested in how redwood compares cost wise, and network/security for private deploys
00:26 Priya: priya product, timeline is q3 pilot and then scale, budget is limited so we care about unit economics
00:34 Sofia: great, quick note - ethan here is our solutions engineer, he'll dive into batching/caching and perf things, i'll cover pricing and commercial flow
00:42 Ethan: yeah hi everyone, quick question to start, what's your current cost per 1k tokens today and typical tokens per request?
00:50 Avery: rough numbers, about $1.80 per 1k tokens on our self-hosted infra factoring in infra and ops, avg request is 750 tokens incl context, peak qps ~45, avg qps ~12
01:05 Sofia: got it, and do you have a target latency SLO for user-facing assistant?
01:10 Priya: sub 300ms 95th ideally, but we accept up to 500ms if quality is better
01:17 Ethan: ok, that's helpful. So on Redwood Hosted our public list pricing for high-capacity seq-models is X (we discussed per-token tiers), but real effective cost depends on batching and whether you can use prefix/KV cache. For example, per-token list price could be $0.002 / 1k for embeddings, but for gen models it's variable - sorry those numbers are indicative, we'll send sheet.
01:38 Avery: can you walk through an example calc? we want to compare hosted vs dedicated vs private on a per-unit basis including ops overhead
01:45 Ethan: sure - quick hypothetical: assume model generates 750 tokens per request, avg token compute cost on GPU is C_t, but you can amortize overhead via batching. If you average batch size 8 at 12 qps that reduces per-token overhead ~ by 6-7x in our runtime. So list price times (1 - batching efficiency) gives you effective per-token. Also prefix caching: if a lot of the prompt is repeated, our KV cache can avoid recomputing the prefix, so only new tokens incur full compute.
02:10 Marcus: internal note - our prompts have large system prompt of 400 tokens repeated every request, so prefix caching sounds huge for us
02:18 Ethan: exactly, if 400/750 tokens are repeatable and hit cache, you're only paying for the remaining 350 tokens in compute terms. On Dedicated you also remove managed markup and get better throughput per dollar but there's an upfront commit. So math: hosted per-token list price P_host, effective cost = P_host * tokens_new / tokens_total * (1 / batching_efficiency factor) + small overhead for storage/IO. On Dedicated, your effective unit cost is (reserved monthly commit / total tokens expected) + infra + support; tends to be cheaper above a certain volume.
02:48 Sofia: to add - customers we see at 5-10B tokens/month usually start saving with Dedicated; below that Hosted often wins due to no commit. But depends on latency tolerance + security needs.
03:00 Avery: our run rate approx 1.2B tokens/month projected in q3, is that in the break-even?
03:06 Ethan: you're in the range where Dedicated could be interesting. We'll run simple break-even calc: need your expected tokens, expected growth, and preferred commit term. We'll send a sample model: i can estimate cost-per-1k under hosted vs dedicated with your cache hit assumptions.
03:20 Priya: curious about quantization and model variants, could smaller quantized models hit our SLO?
03:26 Ethan: yes, we support quantized runtimes and recommend A/B testing — lower precision can reduce compute significantly but sometimes increases latency slightly depending on kernels. We also have model variants for latency-optimized vs quality-optimized. Our runtime picks kernels to keep latency predictable.
03:40 Marcus: security Qs - if we go private does redwood still manage control plane? we need KMS/HSM, SSO, audit logs
03:48 Sofia: for Private you get a customer-managed control plane option; KMS integrations and audit logs are available. We can share SOC2 docs and private deployment checklist.
03:55 Avery: great, also curious about burst capacity, we have flash events where qps spikes 6x
04:02 Ethan: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst pools. For Hosted we have routing policies and fallbacks to compatible model variants; we can also provision burst capacity as part of enterprise contracts.
04:12 Priya: ok let's do a concrete example calculation live: say 1.2B tokens/month, avg 750 tokens/request -> approx 1.6M requests. If prefix cache hits 50% of tokens, and batching gives effective 4x efficiency, how does that translate?
04:29 Ethan: rough calc on the call: tokens billed = 1.2B but compute tokens ~ 1.2B * (1 - 0.5) = 600M compute-equivalent tokens; batching 4x -> effective compute cost equivalent to 150M tokens at single-request efficiency; then multiply by per-token price. So if hosted per-1k price is $X, you'd do (150M / 1000) * X. Then add storage/kv overhead and CDN/IO.
05:02 Avery: we have a strict monthly budget cap of $8k for inference to start — is that feasible with hosted?
05:08 Sofia: with 1.2B tokens that budget is likely undersized for full production; but for a pilot scoped smaller (e.g., 100-200M tokens) Hosted can fit easily. Dedicated would require higher budget. We can model a pilot at 150M tokens and show projections to your 1.2B.
05:22 Marcus: can redwood report token-level billing so we can map to product features?
05:27 Sofia: yes our Console has per-route, per-token cost breakdown, token-level traces, latency; we can export to your billing system or send CSVs.
05:34 Priya: what about caching TTL and invalidation? our user context changes frequently
05:40 Ethan: KV cache is configurable by prefix key TTL; you can choose session-based caching (short TTL) and still get wins on repeated system prompts or static knowledge. For highly dynamic user context you might get less hit rate but still benefit from batch and model optimization.
05:55 Avery: any concerns about hallucinations when switching to smaller quantized models?
06:00 Ethan: yes quality tradeoffs exist; we recommend running evals and using our Optimize toolkit which ties quality regressions to prompt sets and alerts.
06:10 Sofia: summary so far - action items: ethan will run a benchmark plan, sofia will send pricing and security docs, avery to provide token volumes and SLOs. we'll do a follow-up benchmark week of 4/20.
06:20 Priya: sounds good. quick other Q - are there any hidden costs e.g. egress charges or storage for kv cache?
06:27 Ethan: for Hosted egress to internet follows cloud provider norms; storage for kv cache is included up to a point, we can size it, there might be small storage fees at very large scale. We'll detail everything in the pricing sheet.
06:38 Avery: timeline constraints - we need a pilot by end of q2 to validate before q3 scale, can you commit to that?
06:45 Sofia: yes we can prioritize a pilot; to do this we need the prompt set and sample traffic and we'll run a 2-week benchmark; ethan will coordinate.
06:52 Marcus: last tech Q - what's the recommended model routing policy when you have a mixture of latency-sensitive and cost-sensitive routes?
07:00 Ethan: route by policy: latency routes to low-latency variants in dedicated or hosted region, cost-sensitive to quantized models or lower tier; fallback policies route to cached responses or smaller models. We can set per-route SLOs in the Console.
07:14 Priya: ok can you also include a couple of example RPS->latency curves and cost tables in the doc?
07:20 Sofia: yes will include curves and example break-even tables.
07:24 Avery: perfect. thanks everyone.
07:26 Sofia: thanks all, we'll follow up with the sheet and bench plan; end call.
